# Genesis Apocryphon Column 18 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 1QapGen (Cave 1), Col. 18 | **Condition:** Nearly destroyed; only scattered words survive

---

**18:1** [...] Abram [...] departed [...] from Ur of the Chaldeans [...]

**18:2** [...] He arrived in Haran [...] and settled there [...]

**18:3** [...] with Terah his father [...] and Lot, his nephew, the son of Haran [...]

**18:4** [...] and Sarai his wife [...] along with all their possessions [...]

**18:5** [...] Then God spoke to Abram [...] Leave your homeland [...]

**18:6** [...] and your family [...] for the land that I will show you [...]

**18:7** [...] I will make you into a great nation [...] and I will bless you [...]

**18:8** [...] So Abram set out [...] just as the LORD had told him [...]

**18:9** [...] heading for the land of Canaan [...] and he crossed over [...]

**18:10** [...]

---

*PNEUMA notes: Column 18 is nearly destroyed. The fragments capture the dramatic moment of Abraham's calling. "Leave your homeland" renders the Aramaic equivalent of lekh lekha in urgent, immediate language. "Set out" conveys purposeful departure. The Apocryphon retells Genesis 11:31-12:5 in first-person Aramaic narrative.*
